topics.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger took $0 to make Twins. How did it become his biggest paycheck?

demand.title: The Greatest Movie Deal In History #arnold #hollywood #billionairemindset #negotiation

topics.hook: Arnold Schwarzenegger agreed to star in a movie for zero dollars. So how did that movie pay him more than Terminator?
topics.angle: Lane 4 (a celebrity's money moving) through a film the viewer knows. For Twins (1988) Schwarzenegger, Danny DeVito and director Ivan Reitman took no salaries so the studio could make it for $16.5M, and took 40% of the film's backend instead. It made $216M at the box office, and Schwarzenegger says it paid him over $40M, more than any film he made. The turn: the no-salary deal was the studio's safe bet, not his. The payoff: a $0 paycheck that came to over twice the whole film's budget.

topics.hook: Elon Musk flies a private jet almost everywhere. But on paper, the jet isn't his.
topics.angle: Lane 4 (a celebrity's money moving). The jet Musk flies is owned and operated by SpaceX, one of his companies, and Tesla, another of his companies, pays SpaceX whenever he uses it for Tesla work: $700,000 in 2023 and $400,000 in 2025, at rates the two companies set (Tesla's filings, a practice since 2016). The same filings show Tesla paying a security company Musk owns $2.4M in 2023 and $4.8M in 2025. The turn: the richest man's biggest luxury is billed between his own companies. The payoff: the security bill, which doubled in two years.
